channels.name: GitHub repository, releases and issue forms
channels.audience: Developers evaluating a self-hostable, open-source world runtime
rules: Follow CONTRIBUTING.md, CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md and SECURITY.md.
Never open promotional issues, mass-comment, or ask for stars.
Release notes only describe changes present in the tagged tree.
Showcase links only to public, reproducible work that the author chose to share.
Record the observable outcome after each action; leave it empty when nothing is observable.
channels.cadence: With a verified release or a real technical change; no fixed posting quota.

channels.name: Hacker News
channels.audience: Engineers and founders who reward technical honesty over marketing
rules: A real person posts from their own account; automation must not post.
No Show HN for a project that cannot be tried, and no reposting the same launch.
Never ask for upvotes or coordinate voting.
Answer technical questions directly; disclose that you maintain the project.
channels.cadence: At most one Show HN per meaningful release; skip if nothing new is testable.

channels.name: Reddit developer and world-building communities
channels.audience: Subreddit-specific; read each community's rules before writing anything
rules: Read and obey each subreddit's self-promotion rules; some forbid it entirely.
Disclose authorship in the post body.
Answer questions in existing threads before considering a standalone post.
No cross-posting the same text to many communities.
channels.cadence: Only where the rules allow it, and only with a genuinely different angle per community.

channels.name: Product Hunt
rules: One launch, run by the owner's account.
No fake reviews, no incentivized upvotes, no purchased placement.
Describe only released and testable capability; label Fixture output.
channels.cadence: At most one launch per major release.

channels.name: Technical blog or dev.to
channels.audience: Developers who want an implementation story, not an announcement
rules: Every claim must cite a repository path or a reproducible command.
Publish the article on an account the owner controls.
Link to the repository once; do not pad with calls to action.
channels.cadence: After a real engineering milestone, with a new lesson worth reading.

channels.name: Open-source ecosystem lists and integrations
channels.audience: Maintainers of adjacent tools and curated lists
rules: Ask the list or project maintainer before submitting; follow their contribution guide.
Only submit when the integration or entry is real and maintained.
Never open an unrelated pull request to place a link.
No bulk outreach or identical messages.
channels.cadence: Only when a genuine integration exists and its maintainer agrees.
